stories.text: A plaque on this house, 38 Manton Crescent in Lenton Abbey, says that the writer Alan Sillitoe was born here on 4 March 1928.

Around 1361 Gervase de Wilford is thought to have founded a church here, and the building dates from the late 14th century; it was restored in 1890–92 by Naylor and Sale.[^s1][^s2] Inside are two memorials to the poet Henry Kirke White, who drew much inspiration from Wilford and Clifton.[^s1]

stories.text: In 1804–05 the young poet Henry Kirke White lived at Wilford Crossroads. He is said to have spent much of his time writing poems in the churchyard, under his favourite tree.
The churchyard holds the war graves of eight soldiers of the First World War and an airman of the Second. Albert Harvey Iremonger, killed in action on 14 July 1943, aged 27, is buried here.
The poet lived in Wilford in 1804–1805; the church holds two memorials to him.[^s1][^s2]

65557.sum: St Wilfrid's Church, Wilford is a Grade II* listed parish church in the Church of England in Wilford, Nottinghamshire, England.

stories.text: Garners Hill, said to be the oldest site in Nottingham, once held cave dwellings, a Saxon fort and a medieval town hall, until the Victorians cleared it for a railway line. On 14 November 2009 an art centre designed by Caruso St John opened here, its walls embossed with a Nottingham lace pattern.

74224.sum: Nottingham Contemporary (formerly known as the Centre for Contemporary Art Nottingham) is a contemporary art centre in the Lace Market area of Nottingham, England. The gallery opened in 2009. The gallery describes its site as being "the oldest in the city", having been the site of a Saxon fort.

stories.text: On the night of 8–9 May 1941 the Luftwaffe bombed Nottingham. Firefighters saved St Mary's Church after an incendiary burned through its roof; three Boots factories, in Poplar Street, Island Street and Station Street, were on fire; University College and the Shakespeare Street chapel were hit. The worst loss was at the Co-op bakery on Meadow Lane, where 49 people died. In all, 159 people were killed that night.

Built in 1877–81 for University College Nottingham, with the town's library and a natural history museum, and damaged by bombs in the Second World War. D. H. Lawrence studied here to become a teacher; it is now Nottingham Trent University's Arkwright Building.
Built between 1877 and 1881 for University College Nottingham, where D. H. Lawrence studied during his teacher-training years.[^s1]

76264.sum: The Arkwright Building is a Grade II* listed university building on Shakespeare Street in Nottingham, England. It forms part of the Nottingham Trent University City Campus and is one of the university's principal historic buildings. Built between 1877 and 1881, the building was originally home to University College Nottingham, the city library and a natural history museum.

stories.text: D. H. Lawrence was born in 1885 at 8a Victoria Street, a brick house of about 1875 and one of the four houses his family lived in in Eastwood.[^s1][^s2] It became a museum in 1976, and is listed Grade II.[^s1]

150608.sum: D.H. Lawrence Birthplace Museum is a museum on Victoria Street. The building dates from about 1875, according to Historic England (via Wikipedia). It is Grade II listed as 8A, Victoria Street.

stories.text: 28 Garden Road, a brick miner's cottage of about 1880 at the end of a row, was another of the Lawrences' homes. It is listed Grade II.

151625.sum: 28, Garden Road is a house on Garden Road. The building dates from about 1880, according to Historic England (via Wikipedia). It is Grade II listed.

stories.text: St Mary Magdalene's stands on the site of a Saxon church.[^s1] Its tower was built in stages between the 12th and 14th centuries, and its porch in 1320.[^s1] Most of the Lords Byron lie in the family vault here, among them the poet Lord Byron, and his daughter Ada, Countess of Lovelace, rests there too.[^s1][^s2] Byron died in Greece on 19 April 1824; Westminster Abbey refused to bury him, and after he lay in state in London he was brought here.[^s2] The church is listed Grade II*.[^s1]

stories.text: A plaque on this house, 79 High Street in Arnold, says that the artist Richard Parkes Bonington was born here on 26 October 1802.

275384.sum: Bonington House, on High Street. Today it houses Arnold Labour Club. The building dates from the 18th century, according to Historic England (via Wikipedia). It is Grade II listed.
